scope: Proposition 7.11 (The exact incidence count) of the manuscript “A torsion-free counterexample to the Kadison–Kaplansky projection conjecture” (preprints/A-Torsion-Free-Counterexample-to-the-Kadison-Kaplansky-Projection-Conjecture-September-23-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 285 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 df6227b615985805), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 35. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Let I = {(Q, x) : Q an indexed copy, x ∈ V (Q)}. There is a canonical bijection I −→ Γproj × V (Y ), (Q, x) 7−→ (x, typeQ(x)), (7.10) where the type is the base vertex under the unique source vertex of the embedding. It intertwines left translation of Γproj with left translation of the first coordinate, with the base type fixed. In particular, for a fixed x ∈ Γproj and v ∈ V (Y ) there is exactly one incidence at x of type v, even when P is disconnected.
